Current-tab automatic cleanup is a different setting, **Archive current tabs** on the Space’s Browsing page on Mac. It archives old unpinned tabs after the chosen interval, keeping them recoverable until the Archive retention policy later expires them.


# Turn Crest Passwords on or off per Space (/guides/crest-passwords-per-space)

Crest Passwords are private to the Space that owns them. You can stop using Crest-owned suggestions, generation, and save prompts in one Space without deleting its saved passwords or changing another Space.

## Change the setting [#change-the-setting]

On Mac:

1. Open **Crest Settings** and select the Space in the sidebar.
2. Select **Passwords**.
3. Turn **Use Crest Passwords** on or off.

On iPhone and iPad:

1. Open **Settings → Passwords**.
2. Choose the Space you want to change from the **Space** menu.
3. Turn **Use Crest Passwords** on or off.

When Crest Passwords is off, saved passwords remain in that Space until you delete them. Turning the setting back on makes them available to matching sites again.

## Related controls [#related-controls]

The same page lists the Space’s saved passwords, with **Import Passwords…** and **Export Passwords…**. When Crest Passwords is on, supported Mac builds can also show:

- **Sync with iCloud Keychain**, which updates whether existing and future Crest credentials in that Space synchronize through the system Keychain.
- **Offer a copy to Passwords**, which lets the system Passwords app ask separately for a copy after Crest saves in the Space.

System Passwords and passkeys are provider-managed and may appear in any Space for a matching site. They are separate from Crest Passwords’ Space-local records. On Mac, check Crest’s access to system passkeys in **Settings → Privacy → System permissions → Passkeys**.

<Callout type="info" title="What turning it off does not do">
It does not delete saved passwords, export them, move them to another Space, or place password values in CloudKit session data.
</Callout>

Private Spaces must be unlocked before Crest reveals account and site metadata or changes their password settings.

## Storage and deletion [#storage-and-deletion]

Crest Passwords are saved in the system Keychain and suggested only for matching websites. Viewing, copying, or exporting a password can require device authentication.

Deleting a saved password, clearing a site's data, and deleting a whole Space are separate actions, and each shows what it removes before it proceeds.


# Customize and arrange Spaces (/guides/customize-spaces)

Open a Space’s context menu to edit it, or open its page in Settings. On Mac, select the Space in the Settings sidebar; on iPhone and iPad, choose it in **Settings → Spaces**. A strong visual identity makes a profile boundary obvious before you type a password or open a work account.

## Choose an identity [#choose-an-identity]

Crest offers two presentation styles:

- **Banner** uses Crest Studio: begin with a template, then choose a shape, field division, pattern, trim, and heraldic artwork. Use independent colors for the parts of your design, or make an identity with an emoji, monogram, or searchable SF Symbol.
- **Traditional Gradient** keeps the familiar Arc-style theme: it blends one to three colors with direction, intensity, a readability fade, and optional texture.

The result appears in the Space picker and browser chrome on Mac, iPad, and iPhone.

Crest Studio is on the Space’s Appearance page. The crest sits on the Space’s own sidebar background, with its colors named by what they paint:

- **Crest:** Field, Second field, Band, Emblem, Border and Edge. A color for a part the crest doesn’t draw is dimmed.
- **Sidebar:** Background, Accent (selected tabs, pins, the address field and the Space picker) and Pattern.

Click or tap a color to choose one of the templates’ tinctures or a custom color. Below the crest, work through **Start from**, **Shape**, **Field**, **Band**, **Emblem**, **Border**, **Finish** and **Sidebar**; each step shows your crest with each choice applied. On iPhone, the steps are a list showing what each has chosen; tap one to open it. Choose **Icon** at the top of **Emblem** to use an SF Symbol or emoji instead of a crest. **Shuffle** suggests a new crest in the templates’ colors, and **Undo** steps back through your changes. **Reset Appearance** and **Artwork Credits** are in the **…** menu on the Space’s page.

## Customize folders [#customize-folders]

Choose folder color intensity and text color on the Space’s Appearance page. Individual folder menus let you set colors, search the full SF Symbols catalog, or choose emoji. You can show a custom icon on its own instead of the animated folder artwork. In **Settings → Appearance**, enable **Tint Folder Title** to use semibold titles in the folder’s color, adjusted for stronger contrast against light or dark sidebars.

## Customize the browser around your Spaces [#customize-the-browser-around-your-spaces]

Open **Settings → Appearance** for device-wide appearance: a left- or right-side sidebar, borderless pages, tab shape and scale, pinned-tab layout, address-field colors, and a default page zoom from **50% to 300%**. Selected tabs, pins, and the address field follow the current Space’s color; turn off **Follow Space accent** to pick a custom color instead. Presets and a live preview help you find a starting point; each changed setting has its own reset.

Choose an app icon palette here too. These controls change the browser on this device; a Space’s identity belongs to that Space and stays on its own Appearance page.

## Add and arrange Spaces [#add-and-arrange-spaces]

On Mac, click **+** next to the Spaces heading in the Settings sidebar to add a Space. Its Appearance page opens with the name ready to type. Right-click a Space there, or use the **…** menu on its page, to rename it, edit its crest, lock it, or delete it. Crest needs at least one Space.

Drag a Space in the picker to reorder it. In the Mac Settings sidebar, click the pencil next to the Spaces heading, drag Spaces by their handles, then click the checkmark; or right-click a Space and choose **Move Up** or **Move Down**. On iPhone and iPad, use the order controls in **Settings → Spaces**. Position matters for **Control-1** through **Control-9**, so put frequently used Spaces first.

## Automatic cleanup [#automatic-cleanup]

Each Space can archive unpinned current tabs after **12 hours, 24 hours, 7 days, or 30 days**, or keep them until you close them. On Mac, set this with **Archive current tabs** on the Space’s Browsing page, and choose **Archive Now** to run it right away. Cleanup moves tabs into the recoverable Archive; it does not silently erase them.

Pinned sites, saved tabs, folders, and tabs marked **Keep Loaded** have different roles from ordinary current tabs. Use a saved tab for something you intend to revisit, and Keep Loaded only when the live in-page state matters.


# Organize tabs, saved pages, and folders (/guides/organize-tabs-and-folders)

Crest uses a few distinct kinds of tab so temporary work and lasting structure do not become the same pile.

## Current tabs [#current-tabs]

An ordinary page appears in the current-tabs area. Close or archive it when finished, or let the Space’s cleanup policy move old unpinned tabs into Archive.

## Pinned sites [#pinned-sites]

Pinned sites appear as a compact icon grid near the top of a Space. Use them for always-close destinations such as mail, calendar, or a dashboard. Choose **Pin or Unpin Current Tab** or press **Command-D**. You can also right-click a tab and choose **Pin Tab**, or right-click a pinned tab and choose **Unpin Tab**; on iPhone and iPad, touch and hold the tab instead.

## Saved tabs and saved locations [#saved-tabs-and-saved-locations]

A saved tab belongs to the durable sidebar, optionally inside a folder. Its saved location is a home URL: you can navigate away, then double-click the saved-location indicator or use the context menu to return home. The context menu can replace or reset that saved location.

## Folders [#folders]

Folders work in both Saved and Current Tabs. Rename them, choose a color or symbol, collapse them, nest them, and reorder their contents. Drag a complete folder between the two sections to move its tabs and nested folders together. You can also use the folder menu to change sections.

Both kinds restore and sync with their section. Moving a folder preserves its name, color, hierarchy, and contents. Drag a tab onto another current tab to create a folder, or use its context menu to create or choose a folder.

When an extension groups tabs, as Claude does with the tabs it works in, the group appears as a current folder with the group's name and color. Editing that folder changes the group the extension sees. See [Extension compatibility](/guides/extension-api-compatibility/).

Drop along a folder’s top or bottom edge to place a tab beside it, including between empty folders. Drop inside the folder to file the tab.

## Context-menu actions [#context-menu-actions]

Right-click on Mac or touch and hold on iPhone and iPad. Depending on the item, Crest offers rename, copy link, change icon, pin, save, move to Space, add to Split View, duplicate, unload, Keep Loaded, close, archive, reset saved location, or delete.

## Tab icons [#tab-icons]

A tab's icon normally follows the current website. From the tab's context menu, choose **Pull New Icon** to keep the website's current icon, **Change Icon…** to choose an emoji, or **Clear Icon** to return to the automatic website icon.

## Organize several items at once [#organize-several-items-at-once]

Select tabs, Split View groups, and folders together to organize them in one step. On Mac, **Command-click** toggles individual items and **Shift-click** selects a range. Use the selected items’ context menu for the available batch actions, or drag the selection to its destination.

On iPhone and iPad, use the selection actions in a tab or folder’s context menu. VoiceOver exposes selection actions too. A selected folder carries its nested contents with it.

## Clear open tabs [#clear-open-tabs]

Use the archive control on the sidebar divider to clear open tabs while keeping pinned and saved tabs. Closed tabs remain recoverable in Archive, subject to the Space’s retention settings.

## Keep Loaded and unload [#keep-loaded-and-unload]

**Keep Loaded** protects an important live page from ordinary unloading. It is useful for an unsaved editor, a live call, or a dashboard whose in-page state matters. Crest can still respond to genuine system memory pressure.

Choose **Unload** when you want to release a page but retain its tab. On Mac, middle-clicking a current tab closes it; middle-clicking a pinned or saved item unloads its page while keeping the durable item.


# Browse with a Private Space (/guides/private-spaces)

Create a Private Space when the browsing session should not become part of normal durable browser state.

Private Spaces use non-persistent website storage. They stay out of normal history, session restoration, Archive, and ordinary Crest sync. Closing the private session discards its transient pages and website data.

## Add device authentication [#add-device-authentication]

You can require Touch ID, Face ID, or the device passcode before opening a protected Private Space. On Mac, turn on **Require Touch ID or password** on the Space’s Privacy page in Settings. Crest can relock protected content when the app leaves the foreground so another person cannot return to it from the app switcher.

## What private browsing does not do [#what-private-browsing-does-not-do]

Private browsing does not make you anonymous to websites, your network, an employer, or an internet provider. Files you download and information you deliberately share with a site can still leave the browser. Use the feature to control local browser persistence, not as a promise of network anonymity.


# Spaces and profile isolation (/guides/spaces-and-isolation)

A Crest Space is not only a group of tabs. It is a separate browsing profile with its own durable organization, runtime, and privacy boundary.

## What belongs to one Space [#what-belongs-to-one-space]

- Signed-in website sessions, cookies, caches, local storage, and other website data. On Mac, Chromium and WebKit each keep their own copy for the Space, so a sign-in in one engine does not carry to the other.
- Current, pinned, saved, grouped, and archived tabs
- Nested folders and saved locations
- History, Archive, download records, and their retention choices
- Crest Passwords and optional iCloud Keychain participation
- Site permissions and content-blocking choices
- Extensions, actions, permissions, and extension settings on Mac
- Name, symbol, gradient or crest, and sidebar appearance

That means the same website can be signed into different accounts in Work and Personal without those sessions meeting.

## Switch Spaces [#switch-spaces]

Select a Space from the sidebar, swipe or scroll through the Space picker, or use **Option-Command-Left/Right** on a keyboard. **Control-1** through **Control-9** selects a Space by position.

Switching changes the whole browser context. The visible tabs, history search, credentials, permissions, and website process pool all follow the selected Space.

## Move a tab between Spaces [#move-a-tab-between-spaces]

Open the tab’s context menu and choose a destination, or drag it to another Space when the interface presents that destination. Crest moves the durable tab record and loads it inside the destination profile; it does not transfer the source Space’s cookies or signed-in session.

## Delete a Space carefully [#delete-a-space-carefully]

Deleting a Space removes its tabs, pins, folders, Archive, history, Crest Passwords, cookies, website storage, permissions, downloads records, and extension state. Read the confirmation before continuing. If you only need less clutter, archive or move tabs instead.


# Use Split View (/guides/split-view)

Split View keeps two to four live tabs in one durable sidebar group. The focused card owns the address field and page commands; the other cards remain visible and live.

## Create a Split View [#create-a-split-view]

Use any of these paths:

- Drag a sidebar tab onto the current page.
- Open the tab context menu and choose the Split View action.
- Right-click or touch and hold a page link, then choose **Open Link in Split View**.
- Run **Split With Next Tab** from the command palette or assign it a shortcut.

A one-card placeholder lets you add the next tab without losing the first page.

## Focus a card [#focus-a-card]

Click or tap a card. On a keyboard, use **Control-Command-Left** and **Control-Command-Right**. The address, Back and Forward, Reload, Find, Reader, page tools, Peek, and extension popups follow the focused card.

On Mac, turn on **Focus follows pointer** in **Settings → Tabs** to make pointer movement choose the active card automatically.

## Resize and reorder [#resize-and-reorder]

Drag a divider to resize columns on Mac or iPad. Crest remembers widths for the window. Use **Shift-Command-Left/Right** to move the focused card, or drag when the interface exposes a reordering target.

In the sidebar, drag the split's header to move the whole group. Drag an individual tab row to move just that tab out of the split, into a folder, or into another Split View. The remaining tabs stay together.

## Remove or separate tabs [#remove-or-separate-tabs]

**Remove Tab From Split** takes the focused tab out of the group. **Separate All Tabs** turns every card back into an independent tab; its default shortcut is **Option-Command-U**. Closing the focused card closes that tab while the remaining group survives.

## iPad and iPhone [#ipad-and-iphone]

iPad uses the same resizable column model as Mac. On iPhone, the group remains complete but one card fills the screen at a time. Swipe horizontally on the compact toolbar to page between cards; the gesture intentionally does nothing when the current tab is not in Split View.

## Sync behavior [#sync-behavior]

The durable group and its card order can sync with the Space. A receiving device adapts the presentation to its screen instead of flattening the group.


# Sync Crest across devices (/guides/sync-across-devices)

Open **Settings → Sync** and enable **Sync Crest with iCloud** on each device signed into the same Apple Account.

## What sync carries [#what-sync-carries]

Crest synchronizes durable browser structure such as Spaces, tabs, saved folders, Split View groups, appearance, Archive, history, and supported preferences. Mac, iPad, and iPhone then render the same model in an interface suited to the screen.

Password values never enter CloudKit. Each Space’s separate **Sync with iCloud Keychain** switch controls its encrypted Crest Password items. Private Spaces and transient Quick Window or Peek state are not normal synced browsing state.

## Check status [#check-status]

The Sync page shows whether iCloud is available and whether Crest has pending records. Apple does not expose the Apple Account email to Crest, so confirm the account directly in System Settings if two devices do not meet.

## Resolve a conflict [#resolve-a-conflict]

If Crest finds different local and cloud histories, it pauses instead of merging or overwriting silently. Choose **Use This Device** only when its copy should replace iCloud. Choose **Use iCloud** only when the cloud copy should replace this device. Read the confirmation carefully because the selected copy becomes authoritative for subsequent sync.


# Set extension keyboard shortcuts (/guides/extension-keyboard-shortcuts)

Extensions can declare keyboard commands, such as opening their popup. Chromium keeps these shortcuts for each Space's installation, so changing one in Work does not change it in Personal.

## Change a shortcut [#change-a-shortcut]

1. Open **Crest Settings** and select the Space in the sidebar.
2. Select **Extensions**, then **Shortcuts…**. Chromium's extension shortcuts page opens for that Space.
3. Find the extension's command and set, change or clear its shortcut there.

## When a shortcut does nothing [#when-a-shortcut-does-nothing]

Crest's own shortcuts come first. An extension shortcut runs only when no Crest command uses the same keys. Check **Crest Settings → Shortcuts** for a conflict, and pick different keys for one of them.

A shortcut that opens an extension's popup shows it beside the extension's pinned icon, or beside the control that opens the window's extension list when the extension is not pinned.


# Manage permissions and website access per Space (/guides/manage-extension-permissions)

Every Space keeps its own extension installations, permissions and website access. Allowing a tool in Work does not grant it the same access in Personal or on another Mac.

## At installation [#at-installation]

The install review lists the permission warnings Chromium reports for the extension. Where the extension allows it, turn on **Withhold website access until I grant it** so the extension reaches a site only after you allow it. See [Install from the Chrome Web Store](/guides/install-chrome-web-store/).

## Review access later [#review-access-later]

1. Open **Crest Settings** and select the Space in the sidebar.
2. Select **Extensions**.
3. Expand the extension's row to see its **Permissions and Website Access**.

## Change website access [#change-website-access]

In the expanded row, select **Manage Permissions in Chromium**. Chromium's page for that extension opens in the same Space, where you can change its site access and other permissions. The change applies only to this Space's installation.

## Turn an extension off without removing it [#turn-an-extension-off-without-removing-it]

Use the **Enabled** switch on the extension's row. The installation and its data in the Space stay put, ready for when you turn it back on.

## Remove it and its data [#remove-it-and-its-data]

Expand the row, select **Remove Extension**, and confirm **Remove from _Space_**. Crest removes the extension and its data from that Space. Other Spaces are unchanged.

Private Spaces must be unlocked before Crest shows or changes their installed extensions.


# Pin extensions and use extension popups (/guides/pin-extensions-and-popups)

Extension actions belong to the Space. Pin the ones you use often and leave occasional tools in Site Controls.

## Open an extension action [#open-an-extension-action]

1. Select **Site Controls** beside the address field.
2. Find the extension's icon in the extension action area.
3. Select the icon to run its action or open its popup.

A popup opens below the icon you selected, attached to the Crest window. It closes when you click outside it, press Escape, move or resize the window, or switch to another app.

Open the icon's menu for more choices: **Extension Settings…**, **Pin to Toolbar**, **Disable Extension**, **Manage Extension…**, **View on Chrome Web Store** and **Remove Extension…**. In a private window the menu offers only the choices that don't change the Space's installation.

## Pin an action [#pin-an-action]

Select the pin button beside the action in Site Controls, or choose **Pin to Toolbar** from its menu. Pinned icons appear in the Space's own strip below the address field. They stay there on the Start Page too, before you open any page in the Space.

To remove an icon from the strip, choose **Unpin from Toolbar**. Unpinning does not disable or uninstall the extension.

## Open an extension's settings [#open-an-extensions-settings]

If the extension has a settings page, choose **Extension Settings…** from its menu, or expand it on the Space's Extensions page in **Crest Settings** and select **Extension Settings**. The page opens in the Space that owns the installation.

## Use side panels [#use-side-panels]

Extensions with a Chrome side panel open it as a card beside the page. Choose **Open Side Panel** from the action's menu, select the icon if the extension opens its panel that way, or let the extension open it itself. The panel belongs to the page it opened beside. Crest does not keep side panels after you quit.

<Callout type="info" title="Space-local placement">
Pinning is independent per Space and per device. A Work strip can hold work tools while Personal or another Mac uses a different set.
</Callout>


# Crest Help (/guides)

Crest is a browser made of Spaces. It gives work, home, research, and private browsing separate places to live, and switching Spaces changes the browsing context, not just the color of the window. Each Space keeps its own signed-in sessions, cookies, history, tabs, pinned sites, passwords, permissions, website data, appearance, and sync identity.

Crest brings Chromium and WebKit together on Mac. Read the [engine and upgrade guide](/guides/engines/) for website sign-ins, extensions, and choosing an engine. iPhone and iPad continue to use WebKit.

## Crest on each device [#crest-on-each-device]

The same Spaces and browsing model carry across Mac, iPad, and iPhone, while the controls adapt to the screen.

| Device | How Crest fits |
| --- | --- |
| Mac | Chromium and WebKit in one app, the sidebar, Split View with two to four tabs, keyboard-first commands, Quick Window, Peek, extensions, and multiple windows. Signed, notarized releases come directly from GitHub. |
| iPad | The full Space structure, resizable Split View columns, touch navigation, hardware-keyboard commands, and Peek. |
| iPhone | The web page stays primary. The full sidebar becomes its own view, and Split View becomes a pager of focused cards. |
